361538.title: Weakly consecutive sequence generation conjecture
361538.statement: A **weakly consecutive sequence (WCS)** is a permutation $\sigma$ of $\{1,\ldots,k\}$ such that if an integer $d$ divides $\sigma(i)$, then $d$ also divides $\sigma(i\pm d)$ wherever these terms are defined. The paper specifies four starting sequences and three rules for generating WCSs. **Weakly consecutive sequence generation conjecture.** Any WCS can be derived from one of the four starting sequences by applying the three rules. Moreover, for $k\geq 12$, the starting sequence and rule applications are unique up to reordering the rules. This has been verified computationally up to $k=500$, while uniqueness is false for $k\leq 11$; the asserted sufficiency of the starting sequences and rules remains unproved.
361538.review_depth: Section 3 starting sequences/rules; Conjecture 5.1; authors verified k<=500. Selected primary definitions/theorem/proof contexts read; not a comprehensive later-literature audit.
361538.mathematical_attempts: Pairwise WCS is exactly gcd(v_i,|i-j|)=gcd(v_j,|i-j|). Exhaustive small CSP and large residue-signature/transposition neighborhoods were run; a larger-domain CSP was also attempted. A necessary unary residue-cardinality filter was derived to strengthen it. Complete filtered enumeration covers k=501..570 and 851..870 except k=861, which hit its cap. There is also an eight-witness same-family mismatch at k=862. At k=562 the literal family misses four WCSs. Backward check finds the same obstruction at k=22: the explicit witness in WCS-SOURCE-INTERNAL-OBSTRUCTION.md is directly checked on 10648 triples and lies outside the 12-element literal closure. It is obtained by prepending 22 to the already printed length-21 Sophie starting sequence; source Table 2 already records N(22)=16. Thus the source itself contains the ingredients/count discrepancy; this is a routine source-internal bridge/possible omitted family extension, not a qualifying significant endpoint.
361538.remaining_gap: No new discovery claimed. Root may adjudicate intended generator scope; source-internal shortcut and wording-correction exclusions apply. No Lean packet for a corrected or surrogate generation predicate.

354984.title: Complete score conjecture for two-row grids
354984.statement:
Let $G_{2,m}$ be the rectangular grid with two rows and $m$ columns, and let $Ls(G_{2,m})$ and $Rs(G_{2,m})$ denote the corresponding left and right scores. **Two-row grid score conjecture.** For $m\geq 2$,

$$
Ls(G_{2,m})=-Rs(G_{2,m})=
\begin{cases}
6 & \text{if } m=3,\\
4 & \text{if } m\equiv 1 \pmod 2 \text{ and } m\geq 5 \text{ or } m=2,\\
2 & \text{if } m\equiv 0 \pmod 2 \text{ and } m\geq 4.
\end{cases}
$$

The preceding theorem and lemma establish part of this pattern, and the source notes that it remains only to prove $Ls(G_{2,m})\leq 2$ for even $m$; the conjecture was checked computationally up to $m=30$.
354984.review_depth: PDF Section 7.1 Theorem 50, Lemma 51, Conjecture 52. Authors checked m<=30; only even upper bound Ls<=2 remains. Selected primary definitions/theorem/proof contexts read; not a comprehensive later-literature audit.
354984.mathematical_attempts: Exact alternating minimax removes chosen vertex and its neighbors. A second implementation canonicalizes connected ladder components under reflection and sorts their disjoint sum. Both agree on overlapping small grids. The beyond-range m=32 attempt hits its explicit state cap.
354984.remaining_gap: Need upper-bound strategy for every even m, or complete m=32 calculation; no score at m=32 is claimed.

382272.title: The orbit-representation conjecture for integral points of $X_{N,y}$
382272.statement:
Let $N\in\mathbb{N}$ and $y\in\Gamma_N$. Let $\eta\in X_{N,y}(\mathbb{Z})$ be an integral point. For $\widehat{w}\in\Sigma W^0$ and $g\in G$, define the action $g\cdot\widehat{w}$ as in the preceding notation. **Orbit-representation conjecture.** There exist $\widehat{w}\in\Sigma W^0$ and $g\in G$ such that

$$
g\cdot\widehat{w}=\eta.
$$

This conjecture is presented as a natural analogue of the earlier result referred to as the conjecture in the source, and has been checked for the first values of $N$ up to $N=1000$. Its general validity remains open.
382272.review_depth: v1 Conjecture 8.45; current Theorem 8.3, Remark 8.4, Proposition 2.4(2), Lemma 8.10, Table 1, proof in Section 8.5. Selected primary definitions/theorem/proof contexts read; not a comprehensive later-literature audit.

L parametrizes extended Grassmannian elements; G fixes y. Its proof chooses the residue row of Table 1 and applies Lemma 8.10. This covers the intended orbit-surjectivity problem. v1 also has inconsistent affine-coordinate constants, so a literal old-coordinate correction has no credit.

340676.title: Symmetry, unimodality, and factorial sum for diagonal numerators of the blade array
340676.statement:
Let $T^B_{n,k}$ be the array whose entries count blades of dimension $n-k$ in the canonical basis of graduated blades, with diagonal generating functions formed from the corresponding diagonal sequences. Let the numerator polynomial of each such generating function have coefficient vector $(b_1,\ldots,b_m)$, where a vector is symmetric when $b_i=b_{m-i}$ and unimodal when its entries weakly increase to a peak and then weakly decrease. **Diagonal numerator conjecture.** The coefficients of the polynomial numerators of the generating functions for the diagonals of the array $T^B_{n,k}$ are symmetric and unimodal, and sum to the sequence

$$
a(m)=\frac{(2m)!}{m!}.
$$

The conjecture was verified numerically in Mathematica through the 24th diagonal, but a general proof is not given.
340676.review_depth: Proposition 8.3, Conjecture 8.4, Remark 8.5, Appendix A proof by Donghyun Kim. Selected primary definitions/theorem/proof contexts read; not a comprehensive later-literature audit.
340676.mathematical_attempts: Source already proves symmetry and factorial sum. Remaining unimodality was tested exactly through diagonal 100 from the Stirling convolution. A second exact expansion in x^i(1+x)^(j-2i) has nonnegative gamma coefficients through 100. This stronger finite observation suggests an all-j recurrence route.
340676.remaining_gap: Need all-j nonnegative gamma expansion or another full unimodality proof, with the Stirling/diagonal bridge formalized. Source printed symmetry indexing in MathDB is defective and not exploited.
